item.content:encoded:
India ascertaining details of incident involving 14 Indians on yacht off Yemen coast India on Thursday said it was ascertaining details of an incident involving 14 Indian nationals on board a yacht off the coast of Yemen, assuring all possible assistance to ensure their safety and well-being. The statement followed claims by Yemen's Houthis that their forces had launched a rescue operation after what they described as a Saudi attack on the vessel. Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

Country:

Yemen

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

India on Thursday said it was ascertaining details of an incident involving 14 Indian nationals on board a yacht off the coast of Yemen, assuring all possible assistance to ensure their safety and well-being. The statement followed claims by Yemen's Houthis that their forces had launched a rescue operation after what they described as a Saudi attack on the vessel. "We have seen reports regarding an incident involving 14 Indian nationals on board a yacht off the coast of Yemen today. We are ascertaining further details about the incident and will provide all possible help for ensuring the safety and well-being of the Indian nationals," the Embassy of India in Yemen posted on X. Earlier in the day, Yemen's Houthis alleged that Saudi Arabia had targeted an Indian yacht carrying 14 Indian nationals near Zuqar Island in the southern Red Sea, following which their forces initiated a rescue operation. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree, citing preliminary information, stated that the Yemeni Armed Forces would share further details as they became available. "The Saudi enemy is targeting an Indian yacht near Zuqar Island, carrying 14 people of Indian nationality, according to preliminary information. The Yemeni Armed Forces are rescuing them and will provide more details later. This reckless act by the Saudi enemy in targeting it threatens international navigation in the Red Sea, and the international community must stop the Saudi enemy from these reckless actions," Saree had posted on X. The latest development comes a day after an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, Saudi Arabia, killed two people, including an Indian national, while two other Indian nationals sustained injuries, according to the Indian Embassy in Riyadh. India has also strongly condemned the continued attacks on civilian and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, including the strikes on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam and Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oil field. New Delhi also expressed hope for an early restoration of peace and normalcy in the region. "We strongly condemn the continued attacks on civilian and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, including the attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam and Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oil field in the Eastern Province on October 21. These attacks have unfortunately resulted in civilian deaths and injuries," the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said in a statement. Meanwhile, Yemen's Houthis have accused Saudi forces of carrying out air and missile strikes across several Yemeni provinces this week. (ANI)

item.title: US orders removal of China’s DeepSeek AI over national security concerns
item.description: The US government ordered federal agencies to remove DeepSeek AI applications from government systems, citing national security risks, data exposure concerns, and potential ties to Chinese authorities ...
item.content:encoded:
US orders removal of China’s DeepSeek AI over national security concerns The US government ordered federal agencies to remove DeepSeek AI applications from government systems, citing national security risks, data exposure concerns, and potential ties to Chinese authorities. The directives also ban federal departments from using DeepSeek technology in official operations and contracts. ANI | Updated: 22-10-2026 19:05 IST | Created: 22-10-2026 19:05 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The United States has directed federal agencies to remove applications developed by Chinese artificial intelligence company DeepSeek from government computer systems, citing potential national security risks and concerns over the exposure of sensitive information to Chinese authorities, The Epoch Times reported. The restrictions also prohibit federal departments from using DeepSeek technology in official operations and government contracts. According to The Epoch Times, the directives were issued on October 16 by the secretaries of Homeland Security and War, along with the director of national intelligence, under a federal law aimed at addressing security threats associated with government supply chains. A spokesperson for the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) told The Epoch Times that executive agencies are prohibited from installing, accessing or operating DeepSeek applications. Departments have also been instructed to identify and remove any existing installations from government systems. According to the report, the federal contracting database SAM.gov lists DeepSeek under an active exclusion effective October 16, without a specified expiration date. The Epoch Times reported that an earlier directive signed by the Department of Homeland Security on July 24 and made public on October 19 detailed the security concerns underlying the decision. According to The Epoch Times, the department warned that DeepSeek's servers are located in China, where authorities have extensive legal powers to access information held by private companies. This raises concerns that data submitted by American government employees and contractors could be transferred to China, potentially exposing confidential information about federal operations and personnel. Officials also flagged concerns about personal data collection, user tracking and cybersecurity vulnerabilities. In February 2025, cybersecurity firm NowSecure identified several weaknesses in DeepSeek's iPhone application, including unencrypted data transmission, insecure storage of sensitive information and features that could enable user tracking. Researchers also detected connections to infrastructure operated by ByteDance, the Chinese parent company of TikTok. The report said that a separate investigation by the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party in April 2025 accused DeepSeek of transmitting American user data to China and aligning certain artificial intelligence responses with Beijing's censorship policies. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
Indian Embassy and Consulate in Saudi Arabia extending full support to affected pilgrims: MEA India is assisting stranded Umrah pilgrims in Saudi Arabia, with around 3,000 returning home over the past week. The government is coordinating with airlines and tour operators. This follows an airport attack in Dammam that killed two people, including an Indian national, and injured others. ANI | Updated: 22-10-2026 17:33 IST | Created: 22-10-2026 17:33 IST

Surveillance footage shows people standing, right before the moment of an attack at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

India's diplomatic missions in Saudi Arabia are actively engaging with concerned airlines and tour operators to facilitate the early return of affected pilgrims, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) announced on Thursday. Tragedy struck on Wednesday when an attack on King Fahd International Airport in Saudi Arabia's Dammam resulted in the death of an Indian national among two fatalities, alongside two other Indian nationals sustaining injuries. According to official figures released by the MEA, approximately 3,000 stranded Umrah pilgrims have travelled back to India over the past week, utilising available flights. "This is in addition to more than 10,000 normal Umrah pilgrims who were booked on the available flights and have travelled back to India over the past week," the ministry stated. "Arrangements are being discussed to facilitate the return of other Umrah pilgrims at the earliest. Our Embassy and Consulate, with the support from community volunteers, are extending all possible welfare assistance. 24×7 Control Rooms have been established to help Indian nationals and regular advisories are being issued." Earlier in the day, the Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia confirmed that it was gathering further details and reaching out to the families affected following the Dammam airport attack. "Saudi authorities have informed that one Indian national was among two people who unfortunately lost their lives in the attack on Dammam airport yesterday night and two Indian nationals were injured. We are ascertaining further details and contacting the affected families. Our thoughts and prayers are with the family and loved ones of the deceased and we wish speedy recovery of the injured," the embassy noted in a post on X. Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) reported that Wednesday's attack targeting the facility claimed two lives, comprising one Indian resident and one Saudi citizen, while leaving eight individuals injured. Providing a comprehensive breakdown via X, the Saudi civil aviation authority clarified, "Further to its earlier statement regarding the attack that targeted King Fahd International Airport in Dammam on the evening of Wednesday, October 21, 2026, corresponding to 10 Jumada Al-Awwal 1448 AH, the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) clarifies that the number of fatalities has risen to (2) after an additional fatality was confirmed, involving (1) Saudi citizen and (1) Indian resident. The number of the injured remains at (8), including (1) Saudi citizen, and residents of the following nationalities: (2) Indian, (2) Yemeni, (2) Bangladeshi and (1) Nepalese. Their injuries range from minor to critical, and they are receiving the necessary medical care at several hospitals." The Saudi civil aviation authority added that it is coordinating closely with relevant departments to evaluate structural damage, verify facility safety, protect personnel and passengers, and uphold the security of the national aviation network. Operations at the airport have since resumed, alongside the restoration of normal air traffic flows. Meanwhile, New Delhi issued a strong condemnation of ongoing attacks directed at civilian and energy infrastructure within Saudi Arabia, encompassing the Dammam airport strike and an incident at Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oil field, while voicing hope for a swift return to peace and normalcy across the region. "We strongly condemn the continued attacks on civilian and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, including the attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam and Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oil field in the Eastern Province on October 21. These attacks have unfortunately resulted in civilian deaths and injuries," the MEA stated. Reaffirming New Delhi's firm stance, the ministry added, "We also reiterate that the attacks on civilian and critical infrastructure are completely unacceptable and must cease immediately. We stand in solidarity with the people and the Government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in safeguarding its sovereignty, and hope that peace and normalcy would return to the region at the earliest." (ANI)

item.description: "The Canadian government brushes off concerns about potential interference in U.S. elections, even as its ministers and premiers openly describe plans to influence American politics in official ...
item.content:encoded:
US accuses Canada of seeking to influence 2026 midterm elections "The Canadian government brushes off concerns about potential interference in U.S. elections, even as its ministers and premiers openly describe plans to influence American politics in official documents and public appearances," the embassy said in the fact sheet. ANI | Updated: 22-10-2026 10:37 IST | Created: 22-10-2026 10:37 IST

US President Donald Trump and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

The United States has accused Canada of seeking to influence American politics ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, the US Embassy Ottawa said in a factsheet. The US Embassy in Ottawa cited statements by Canadian ministers and provincial leaders on retaliatory tariffs, political pressure on the Trump administration and engagements with US Democratic officials. In a factsheet titled “Monitoring Canadian Activities in U.S. Politics”, the embassy alleged that the Canadian government had dismissed concerns about potential interference in American elections despite its officials publicly discussing efforts to exert political pressure in the United States. “The Canadian government brushes off concerns about potential interference in U.S. elections, even as its ministers and premiers openly describe plans to influence American politics in official documents and public appearances,” the embassy said in the factsheet. The factsheet cited Canadian Industry Minister Mélanie Joly’s meetings with US Democratic officials in Boston and Chicago in September 2026, ahead of the midterm elections. When asked about the potential implications for tariffs if Democrats won the elections, Joly reportedly said, “That’s exactly why I’m meeting so many governors and potential presidential candidates,” according to a September 19 report by La Presse Canadienne cited in the document. The embassy also highlighted Joly’s remarks at an August 25 press conference, in which she acknowledged targeting products that would put political pressure on US states. “We’re also targeting products that will target states in the U.S. And so we’re being wise and strategic to put political pressure, and that’s why we think it’s the right thing to do right now,” Joly said, according to the factsheet. It further cited her March 2025 remarks about putting pressure on American businesses in key Republican states to influence the Trump administration. Ontario Premier Doug Ford also featured in the document. The embassy referred to a letter Ford sent to Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney in August 2026, urging consideration of additional retaliatory tariffs on imports from politically significant states supporting the US administration. The factsheet also mentioned Ontario’s CAD 75 million anti-tariff advertising campaign launched in October 2025, which featured excerpts from former US President Ronald Reagan. Ford had said the campaign's message would be repeated across Republican districts nationwide. Other examples included Canadian Liberal MP Anthony Housefather’s reported campaigning for US Democratic Representative Debbie Wasserman Schultz ahead of her Florida primary and Canadian Consul General Bernadette Jordan’s appearance alongside Democratic lawmakers at a Vermont roundtable on trade tensions in October. Separately, the embassy cited US Department of Justice cases involving Canadian citizens charged with or convicted of unlawful voting in American elections. It claimed that at least 11 Canadians had been charged or sentenced in 2026 in cases involving elections and primaries held between 2012 and 2024. The embassy urged Canadians to refrain from participating in or influencing American elections, stating, “All Canadians should refrain from attempting to participate in or influence U.S. elections in any way. Americans decide America’s elections.” The allegations come amid an ongoing trade dispute between Washington and Ottawa that began after US President Donald Trump imposed tariffs on Canadian goods during his second term in 2025, prompting Canada to introduce retaliatory duties. The factsheet adds to tensions between the two countries ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, which will determine control of the US Congress. (ANI)
